title: True, false and truth tables
summary: Conditions are values: true or false, combined with AND, OR and NOT. Delve gets the rules for its locked stairs.

steps.title: Every question has two answers
body: A **boolean** is a value that is either `true` or `false`. Every comparison produces one:
Booleans are values like any other: you can store them in boxes and print them. Naming a boolean well (`isAdult`, `hasTicket`) turns a cryptic condition into a sentence.

steps.explain: C# prints booleans as `True` and `False`. 15 is not at least 18, but it is at least 13.

steps.title: AND, OR, NOT
body: Three operators combine booleans. The spelling varies; the logic never does.
| Idea | C#, Java, JavaScript | Python | True when |
| AND | `a && b` | `a and b` | **both** are true |
| OR | `a \|\| b` | `a or b` | **at least one** is true |
Note that OR is *inclusive*: true OR true is true.

steps.prompt: Match each expression to its value.
`&&` binds tighter than `||`, just as `*` binds tighter than `+`. What is printed?
steps.explain: The first is `a || (b && c)`, which is `true || false`. Parentheses change it to `true && false`.

steps.prompt: With `x = 7`, is each condition true or false?
A ride allows riders who are at least 120 cm tall **and** under 200 cm. Fill the operators so `150` prints `True`.
steps.explain: Both checks must hold, so it is `&&`. A range check is always *lower bound AND upper bound*.

steps.prompt: A shop gives a discount to students **or** people over 65. Which condition is right?
steps.explain: Either reason is enough, so OR. AND would only reward retired students.

steps.title: Leap years
prompt: Write `bool IsLeap(int year)` as a **single boolean expression** (no `if`).
A year is a leap year if it is divisible by 4, **except** years divisible by 100, which are only leap years if also divisible by 400.
hints: Two ways to be a leap year: divisible by 4 but not by 100, *or* divisible by 400.

steps.title: Delve's door rules
prompt: Each Delve floor ends in stairs behind a door. Write the rules as **single boolean expressions** (no `if`, no `?`):

**`static bool CanOpenDoor(bool locked, bool hasKey, bool bossFloor, bool bossDefeated)`**: the door opens when it is **not locked or you have the key**, **and** it is **not on a boss floor or the boss is defeated**. Fill in the truth table on paper first for the boss half:
**`static bool IsMonster(char tile)`**: true for the map tiles `'g'` (goblin), `'m'` (mimic) and `'D'` (dragon).
**`static bool IsItem(char tile)`**: true for `'$'` (chest), `'k'` (key) and `'+'` (potion).
A `char` is one character in single quotes; compare it with `==` like a number: `tile == 'g'`.
starter: static bool CanOpenDoor(bool locked, bool hasKey, bool bossFloor, bool bossDefeated)
solution: static bool CanOpenDoor(bool locked, bool hasKey, bool bossFloor, bool bossDefeated)
template: Dojo.Eq("an unlocked door on a quiet floor opens", true, CanOpenDoor(false, false, false, false));
Dojo.Eq("a locked door without the key stays shut", false, CanOpenDoor(true, false, false, false));
Dojo.Eq("a locked door with the key opens", true, CanOpenDoor(true, true, false, false));
Dojo.Eq("the key is not enough while the dragon lives", false, CanOpenDoor(true, true, true, false));
Dojo.Eq("key and dragon defeated: it opens", true, CanOpenDoor(true, true, true, true));
Dojo.Eq("dragon defeated but no key", false, CanOpenDoor(true, false, true, true));
Dojo.Eq("unlocked, but the dragon lives", false, CanOpenDoor(false, false, true, false));

forbid.message: One boolean expression per function: no if, no ?
Every function starts with `static` (Delve keeps its pieces in one static class)

hints: Each half of the door rule is an OR: "not locked OR has the key". Then AND the halves together.
Use parentheses around each half: `&&` binds tighter than `||`, so without them the expression means something else.

build.title: Door rules
build.unlocks: Delve knows what a monster is, what an item is, and when the stairs open.
